title: Choose the visual world for the Project 27 app
question: The roll assigned the Specimen Cabinet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Specimen Cabinet
options.lineage: natural-history collection drawers: enamelled steel cabinets, unit trays, pinned specimens with typed accession labels
options.thesis: Every candidate solution is a specimen: pinned where it was found, labelled with its value, filed by generation.
options.viewport: A cabinet-green rail holds the four pages and the run controls; the main tray shows the 2-D landscape with the population pinned on it, the best specimen's accession label beside it, and the convergence strip below.
options.risk: Tips into museum costume (wood, brass, aged paper) if pushed past type, palette and pins; held to a clean product grid it stays a working tool.

raised.raise: One plot owns each page's field; every other element is secondary to it.
Every number is set in tabular monospace figures, so errors, FEs and generations line up in columns.
One grotesque carries every heading, label and caption.
A run lands as a complete state: default runs finish before the eye leaves the button.

options.label: Survey Sheet
options.lineage: Swiss topographic survey maps: shaded relief, hypsometric tints, trig-point benchmarks
options.thesis: The landscape is the map; the population is the survey party working across it.
options.viewport: Top tabs for the four pages; the landscape drawn as a tinted relief map with individuals as survey triangles and the optimum as a trig-point benchmark.
options.risk: The literal reading of 'fitness landscape' and the direction most runs on this brief land on; map browns can muddy the chart series.

options.label: Construction Grid
options.thesis: One visible cell grid is the armature for the controls, the charts and the search domain itself.
options.viewport: Sidebar and main area snap to one visible blue cell grid; the 2-D domain is drawn on the same cells; grid-built numerals show the best error.
options.case: Fuses well, since the search domain is literally a grid; loses on audience identification to the cabinet's evolution story.
options.risk: Grid-built numerals read as a gimmick once they leave the one headline number.

options.label: Tabbed Manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with coloured divider tabs
options.thesis: Each page is a manual section with its own divider colour; a stepped tab rail shows where you are.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail on the left, one hue per page; content sits on a pale leaf over that page's divider colour.
options.case: Fuses with strong clarity (colour equals page); loses on audience identification, as examiners no longer read boxed manuals.
options.risk: Six section hues compete with the chart's data colours.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every run filed by catalogue number, its convergence drawn as a stacked pulsar plot.
options.viewport: A black field with 30 runs stacked as white convergence lines and a catalogue index.
options.case: Fuses poorly: colour codes instead of labels fail an examiner working alone.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: The search shown as a strobing black-and-white field of every evaluation.
options.viewport: Barcode columns of evaluations with a sine trace of convergence.
options.case: Fuses poorly: without colour, GA and MA cannot be told apart.

options.label: Annual Plates
options.thesis: Each chart presented as a printed plate with registration marks.
options.viewport: One sheet of plates with crosshair corners and a mono token bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the editorial hairline look is a common default and says nothing about evolution.

options.label: Full-screen Feed
options.thesis: One run fills the screen and the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: A full-viewport landscape with a right rail of glyph controls.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a tool needs its controls and data side by side.
options.kept: Results land as complete states, instantly.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean Streamlit dashboard, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A sidebar of sliders and selects; the main area holds charts and metric tiles.
canonCard.risk: Looks like most student Streamlit projects by design.
